```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
```

This vignette states, for every model of mortensor, the model equation,
the estimation method, how the forecast is generated, the defaults, and
which sources of uncertainty the forecast draws contain. It is meant as
the basis of a methods section. `summary()` of a fitted model prints the
same information for the actual fit, `mt_parameters()` returns the
estimates.

```{r}
library(mortensor)
x <- mt_example(deaths = "single", years = 1995:2019)
summary(mt_fit(lee_carter(), x))
```

Notation: `m(x,t,i)` is the central death rate at age `x` in year `t` in
stratum `i` (deaths divided by exposure), `D` deaths, `E` exposures.

## Data steps that affect every model

| Step | What mortensor does | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Exposures | mid-year population, or the mean of two 1 January or 31 December populations | `mt_as_exposure(type = )` |
| Suppressed cells | raking (iterative proportional fitting; Deming and Stephan 1940) of the missing counts to published totals, within optional bounds | `mt_fill_suppressed()` |
| Unknown ages | distributed over the age groups of the same stratum and year in proportion to the known deaths | `mt_data()` |
| Ungrouping | penalised composite link model with exposures (Rizzi, Gampe and Eilers 2015) or spline methods | `mt_ungroup()`, `step_ungroup()` |
| Smoothing | Poisson P-splines (Currie, Durban and Eilers 2004) or Whittaker smoothing of log rates over age; age 0 is not smoothed | `mt_smooth()`, `step_smooth()` |
| Zero deaths | models on log rates use 0.5 deaths in a cell without deaths | |

All preprocessing steps given as `prep` are refitted on every training
window of a backtest.

## Single-population models

### Lee-Carter: `lee_carter()`

`log m(x,t) = a(x) + b(x) k(t)`, with `sum b(x) = 1` and `sum k(t) = 0`
(Lee and Carter 1992).

* **Estimation**: Poisson maximum likelihood (default; Brouhns, Denuit
  and Vermunt 2002) or SVD of the log rates with `k(t)` refitted so that
  the fitted deaths match the observed deaths (`method = "svd"`, as
  `demography::lca()`). Age groups without any death get a constant rate
  of 0.5 deaths over the training period and `b(x) = 0`; when the Poisson
  likelihood has no finite maximum (very sparse counts), `b(x)` is shrunk
  towards equal shares by a ridge penalty. Both are reported as warnings.
* **Forecast**: `k(t)` follows a random walk with drift; the drift and
  the innovation variance are estimated from the year-to-year changes of
  `k(t)`.
* **Jump-off**: fitted rates of the last year (default) or observed rates
  (`jump_off = "observed"`).
* **Uncertainty in the draws**: innovations of `k(t)` and the uncertainty
  of its drift. `a(x)` and `b(x)` are fixed; `bootstrap = TRUE` or
  `bootstrapped()` adds their uncertainty.

### Random walk with drift: `rwd()`

Each age: `log m(x,t) = log m(x,t-1) + mu(x) + e(x,t)`.

* **Estimation**: drift as the mean year-to-year change (over the last
  `drift_window` years); innovations are resampled vectors of observed
  changes across ages (`innovations = "bootstrap"`, keeps the correlation
  between ages) or normal (`"gaussian"`).
* **Uncertainty**: innovations and drift. The observed changes contain the
  Poisson noise of two years, so the intervals are wide where deaths are
  few, and over long horizons very wide.
* **`observation_noise = TRUE`**: log rate = level + noise, the level a
  random walk with drift (local level model). The noise variance is the
  Poisson part (one over the deaths) plus an extra part common to all ages;
  the level variance is estimated from the variance and first
  autocovariance of the changes and partly pooled across ages (ages with
  few deaths borrow from the median of the others). The level is Kalman
  filtered; draws include level, drift and, for predictive draws, noise.

### Functional demographic model: `hyndman_ullah()`

Calls `demography::fdm()` (Hyndman and Ullah 2007): smoothed log rates
decomposed into a mean function and functional principal components,
whose scores are forecast with time-series models. Draws are simulated
from the fitted model. Its intervals are those of the simulated paths,
which are somewhat narrower at short horizons than demography's analytic
intervals (see the comparison vignette).

### StMoMo models: `stmomo()`

Calls `StMoMo::fit()` and `simulate()` (Villegas, Kaishev and
Millossovich 2018) for the Lee-Carter, CBD, APC, RH and M6 families. Draws
contain the period and cohort index uncertainty that StMoMo simulates;
parameter uncertainty is not included.

### Bayesian age-period-cohort model: `apc_bayes()`

Calls `bamp::bamp()` (Schmid and Held 2007): logit death probability =
age + period + cohort effects with random-walk priors of order 1 or 2,
binomial likelihood, MCMC. Convergence is checked with the Gelman-Rubin
statistic of the identified quantities (reported by `mt_parameters()` as
`rhat`); chains that have not converged are refitted with longer runs.
**Uncertainty**: the posterior predictive distribution, including
parameter uncertainty. `apc_select()` compares random-walk orders by DIC.

## Models for several populations

### Li-Lee: `li_lee()`

`log m(x,t,i) = a(x,i) + B(x) K(t) + b(x,i) k(t,i)` (Li and Lee 2005).

* **Estimation**: the common factor `B(x) K(t)` is a Lee-Carter model
  (SVD, `k` refitted to deaths) of the pooled deaths and exposures of the
  strata in a group (`common_by`, for example one common factor per sex);
  the stratum factors come from an SVD of the residual log rates.
* **Forecast**: `K(t)` random walk with drift; each `k(t,i)` an AR(1)
  process without intercept, `|phi| <= 0.99`, so the deviations of a
  stratum from the common trend stay bounded ("coherent" in the sense that
  the strata do not diverge).
* **Uncertainty**: innovations and drift of `K(t)`, innovations of the
  AR(1) processes (independent across strata). `a`, `b`, `B` and `phi`
  are fixed.

### Product-ratio: `product_ratio()`

The same structure on the geometric mean of the strata (common factor)
and their ratios to it (Hyndman, Booth and Yasmeen 2013), with
Lee-Carter components in place of functional data models.

### Tucker3 and cause shares (experimental)

`tucker3()` decomposes the array of log rates `[age, period, stratum]`;
`cause_shares()` forecasts all-cause mortality and the shares of causes
with a tensor model of their log-ratio coordinates. Neither has a published
evaluation for mortality; compare them with the models above in a
backtest.

## Combining models

### Ensembles: `ensemble()`

A mixture of the predictive distributions of its components: each draw
comes from one component, for all strata at once, chosen with
probabilities equal to the weights (equal, inverse CRPS of an inner
backtest, or stacking). The mixture contains the uncertainty of each
component and the disagreement between them.

### Reconciled forecasts: `reconciled()`

Forecasts of all nodes of a hierarchy (bottom strata and their totals)
are made to add up draw by draw: bottom-up sums, or projections of the
base forecasts with weights from their variances (WLS), the shrunk
covariance (MinT; Wickramasuriya, Athanasopoulos and Hyndman 2019), the
structure (Hyndman et al. 2011) or equal weights (OLS). Deaths add up over
every hierarchy variable; exposures add up over variables that divide the
population and are shared by the levels of variables such as causes of
death (`additive = "rates"`). The exposures of the forecast years are
those of the last observed year unless projections are given.

### Bootstrap and tuning: `bootstrapped()`, `tuned()`

`bootstrapped()` refits a model to Poisson resamples of the deaths
(parameter uncertainty, including preprocessing with `type = "data"`).
`tuned()` chooses settings (for example the rank) by an inner
rolling-origin backtest on the training data only. The fitting period
matters for Lee-Carter forecasts when the pace of decline changed (Booth,
Maindonald and Smith 2002); `step_window(years)` makes it a preprocessing
step that a backtest compares across windows.

## Sources of uncertainty at a glance

| Model | Index innovations | Drift | Parameters | Poisson noise | Extra noise |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lee_carter()` | yes | yes | with `bootstrap = TRUE` | predictive draws | predictive draws |
| `rwd()` | yes (observed changes) | yes | no | contained in the changes | contained in the changes |
| `rwd(observation_noise = TRUE)` | yes (level) | yes | no | predictive draws | predictive draws |
| `li_lee()`, `product_ratio()` | yes (common and stratum) | common factor | no | predictive draws | predictive draws |
| `hyndman_ullah()` | yes | as fdm | no | predictive draws | model error |
| `stmomo()` | yes | yes | no | predictive draws | no |
| `apc_bayes()` | yes | posterior | yes (posterior) | yes | with `overdispersion = TRUE` |
| `ensemble()` | of the components | of the components | of the components, plus model choice | | |

Predictive draws (`predictive = TRUE`, always used in backtests) describe
observable rates: Poisson deaths given the exposures, and for models of
smooth rates an extra-Poisson part estimated from the in-sample residual
variance. Forecast draws without it describe the underlying rates.

## Evaluation

`mt_backtest()` refits preprocessing and model at each origin and scores
predictive draws against the observed log rates of the test years with the
continuous ranked probability score (CRPS; Gneiting and Raftery 2007), the
weighted interval score (Bracher et al. 2021), interval coverage, the
probability integral transform and the absolute error of the median. Cells
with estimated (suppressed) deaths are not scored unless
`score_estimated = TRUE`.
